title: Observability Roadshow Retro and Action Generator
summary: This is a lightweight retro + action-generator from the observability "roadshow" we ran with product, SRE, and two customer success accounts (Jan 2026). Purpose: capture recurring asks, surface cross-team instrument gaps, and produce a prioritized, experimentally-driven action list we can hand to feature owners and the dashboard guild.
notes-to-self:
- meant to be a working doc — copy into confluence after approvals
- keep experiments ≤ 6 weeks where possible so we can iterate quickly
what happened on the roadshow (high leve:
- 7 internal demos + 2 customer sessions; common themes emerged quickly: unclear ownership for per-route token-cost panels; lack of trace anchors for multi-model fanout; operators asking for a compact "slow token" microdash for oncall; product PMs wanted a canary-level SLO that’s cheaper to compute.
- concrete asks: cheaper canaries, one-click drill from dashboard to trace, per-tenant cold-cache view, ability to surface KV-cache warmth by route and model-version.
Recurring pain points (ranked by frequen:
1) Metric provenance / ownership unclear on many panels — operators unsure who to ping
2) Trace-to-panel linkage missing (traces exist but not anchored to the dashboard in a discoverable way)
3) Cost signals (per-token compute cost) mixed with latency metrics; teams want orthogonal views
4) SLI definitions vary by team: we need a small set of canonical SLI contracts for inference: token-ttft, p99-token-latency, attach/fanout-latency, kv-cache-warmth
5) Sampling budget and privacy concerns (customer sessions raised PII and PHI trace redaction questions)
Proposed canonical metrics (short defini:
- ttf-token-mean: mean time-to-first-token from request arrival to first emitted token (ms). Tag by route, model, tier.
- p99-token-latency: 99th percentile per-request token emission time (ms) measured at edge microservice before GPU handoff.
- kv-cache-warmth: fraction of requests that served >= X tokens from KV cache (0–1). X candidates: 16, 64. Store as separate metrics: kv_warmth_16, kv_warmth_64.
- fanout-multimodel-latency: time between initial request and final model result when routing to multiple model variants (ms). Tag by fanout-set id.
- per-token-cost-estimate: aggregated estimate derived from GPU-seconds-per-token * instance-cost; reported as normalized units per 1k tokens.
- trace-sampling-rate-applied: sampling probability used for the request (for downstream reconstruction).
Tracing heuristics recommended (operator:
- Adaptive severity-weighted sampling: always sample 100% for errors, 50% for tail latency > p95, 1% baseline otherwise.
- Anchor spans at three points: ingress (route + request id), model-handoff (model + version + kvcache-hotness boolean), emit (response summary + token_count). These anchors make dashboard drill-to-trace straightforward.
- Redaction policy: PII/PHI fields removed in ingress span. Add a boolean field trace_has_pii that flags when redaction occurred (not contents).
- Sampling budget enforcement: global sampling budget set per-tenant per-day; on budget exceed fall back to severity-weighted downsampling.
Dashboard composition notes (operator-fi:
- Keep a compact "Oncall Microdash" with 6 panels: overall error rate, p99-token-latency, ttf-token-mean, per-token-cost-estimate (trend), kv-cache-warmth_64, slow-token-examples (link to sampled traces).
- Each panel needs provenance metadata (owner, query id, source metric, last updated, related PR/alert). UI stub: small icon with hover containing that metadata.
- Drill behaviour: click on a row -> trace search pre-populated with request id and time window; prefer opening the trace in the same console tab to reduce context switching.
- Cost vs latency panels should live in a separate "Economics" lane; ops microdash should be cost-agnostic by default.
Experiment matrix (action-generator form:
Experiment | Hypothesis | Success metrics | Owner | Duration | Risk
1) Microdash pilot for oncall | compact 6-panel microdash reduces mean time-to-detect by 30% | MTTR-coded (investigation time), fewer page escalations | Jordan Reyes | 4w | low
2) Anchor-span rollout | Adding model-handoff anchor increases successful trace-led investigations by 40% | fraction of incidents with trace linkage | Samir Gupta | 6w | medium
3) KV-warmth thresholds | kv_warmth_64 correlates better with tail latency than kv_warmth_16 | correlation coefficient improvement > 0.2 | Lena Novak | 3w | low
4) Canary SLI approximation | cheap canary (synthetic probe run per 5m replacing heavy SLI) catches 90% regressions | true_positive_rate vs full SLI | Priya Kapoor | 6w | medium-high
Open questions / edge cases:
- How to compute per-token-cost-estimate for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity? (need a normalization doc)
- Privacy: what exact redaction algorithm do we use to guarantee PHI removal? Legal needs to sign off before enabling high-sample-rate traces for regulated customers.
- Multi-tenant dashboards: should per-tenant cost be behind feature flag? (CS says yes for enterprise)

- [ ] (Maya) Draft per-token-cost normalization doc for Dedicated vs Hosted and circulate to finance — due 2026-02-16
- [ ] (Priya) Schedule legal review for tracing redaction approach and capture sign-off requirements — due 2026-02-20
Communication plan:
- Short roadmap email to product, sres, cs with TL;DR and links to microdash prototype + experiment signup
- Weekly 15m sync for experiment owners (Wed 10am PST) — use #obs-roadshow channel for status updates
retro takeaways (tone):
- Roadshow was high signal — avoid large feature-dumps; focus on low-friction instrumentation changes
- Operators want clear ownership badges and a single button to jump to traces
- PRs that change metrics must update panel-provenance metadata before merge (enforce in PR checklist)
next steps:
1) Owners above implement quick wins and report in weekly sync
2) After experiments complete, synthesize results to a short 1-pager and propose changes to default Dashboard templates
3) Move the canonical SLI definitions into a metrics-contracts page and enforce via instrumentation-lint
